intro: The plain-text protocol of the optical port on the front of most European electricity meters. A technician puts a probe on the port. Laptop and meter exchange short ASCII messages, first at 300 baud, then faster. The meter answers with lines such as 1.8.0(012345.678*kWh): an address, a value and a unit.

signon.title: Sign on
signon.text: The technician puts the optical probe on the meter's front. The laptop sends /?! at 300 baud, 7 data bits, even parity. The meter answers with its maker, its top speed and its model.

select.title: Pick speed and mode
select.text: The laptop picks the normal protocol, 9600 baud and a data readout. After the last byte of this message, both sides switch to 9600 baud.

readout.title: Readout
readout.text: The meter sends its readout list in one message, closed by a BCC check. No password is needed: the list holds only what the utility chose to show.

program.title: Programming mode
program.text: Export energy is not in the list. The laptop signs on again, at 300 baud, and asks for programming mode. The meter asks for a password.

password.title: Password
password.text: The laptop sends the password in clear (P1). The meter accepts it with a single ACK.

read.title: Read and leave
read.text: R1 reads one value by its address. The meter answers with the address, the value and the unit. Then B0 ends the session, and the meter goes back to 300 baud.

frames.ident: Maker EXA, model EM340, up to 9600 baud
frames.ident-2: Maker EXA, model EM340, up to 9600 baud

slash.name: Start
slash.note: / (0x2F) starts the sign-on and the identification.

end-request.name: End
end-request.note: ! (0x21) ends the request. On a line shared by several meters, the meter's address stands between ? and !.

maker.name: Maker
maker.note: EXA: the maker's three-letter code (made up here).

baud-5.name: Top speed
baud-5.note: 5: in mode C, this meter can switch to 9600 baud. 0 would be 300 baud, 6 is 19200.

model.name: Model
model.note: EM340: the model, up to 16 characters chosen by the maker.

ack.name: ACK
ack.note: ACK (0x06) starts the acknowledgement and option select.

protocol.name: Protocol
protocol.note: 0: the normal protocol. 2 would switch to HDLC and DLMS (mode E).

speed.name: Speed
speed.note: 5: switch to 9600 baud, the speed the meter offered.

mode-readout.name: Mode
mode-readout.note: 0: data readout. Right after this message, both sides switch to 9600 baud.

mode-program.name: Mode
mode-program.note: 1: programming mode. The meter will ask for a password.

stx.name: STX
stx.note: STX (0x02): data starts. The BCC counts from the next byte.

a-180.name: Address
a-180.note: 1.8.0: active energy import, all tariffs. The C.D.E part of the OBIS code.

v-180.name: Value
v-180.note: (012345.678*kWh): the value and its unit, between brackets.

v-182.name: Value
v-182.note: (003580.246*kWh). Tariff 1 and tariff 2 add up to the total.

etx.name: ETX
etx.note: ETX (0x03): the message ends. It is the last byte the BCC counts.

bcc-data.name: BCC
bcc-data.note: 0x76: every byte after STX, up to and including ETX, combined with XOR. If it does not match, read again.

soh.name: SOH
soh.note: SOH (0x01): a command message starts. The BCC counts from the next byte, STX included.

p0.name: P0
p0.note: A password request, with an operand.

operand.name: Operand
operand.note: (87654321): a number chosen by the meter. A meter that wants a scrambled password (P2) uses it as a seed. This one takes the password in clear.

bcc-p0.name: BCC
bcc-p0.note: 0x68: XOR of all bytes after SOH, up to and including ETX.

p1.name: P1
p1.note: Here is the password, in clear.

password.name: Password
password.note: (18273645). Anyone watching the optical port can read it.

ack-password.name: ACK
ack-password.note: ACK (0x06): the password is right. Reading and writing are open.

r1.name: R1
r1.note: Read one value, as ASCII text.

ask-280.name: Address
ask-280.note: 2.8.0(): the address to read, with empty brackets.

a-280.name: Address
a-280.note: 2.8.0: active energy export, all tariffs: what the building's solar panels fed into the grid.

bcc-answer.name: BCC
bcc-answer.note: 0x5F: from the byte after STX up to and including ETX.

b0.name: B0
b0.note: Break: the session ends at once.

bcc-b0.name: BCC
bcc-b0.note: 0x71, the letter q. A break is always the same 5 bytes: 01 42 30 03 71.

l-d.name: D · processing
l-d.note: 8: the total over time, so energy.

l-value.name: Value
l-value.note: 012345.678: the digits the meter keeps, with its decimal point.

facts.between: Hand-held unit or laptop → meter, through an optical probe
facts.transport: Infrared port with a magnetic probe; also a 20 mA current loop or RS-232
facts.security: None for a readout. Programming mode: a password, sent in clear
facts.speed: Starts at 300 baud, 7E1; then up to 19200 baud

tips: Set the serial port to 7 data bits and even parity (7E1). At 8N1 the meter sees parity errors and stays silent, and its answers look like garbage.
Switch to the new speed only when the last byte of the ACK message has left. USB adapters buffer data: switching too early sends the end of the message at the wrong speed.
The BCC starts after STX or SOH, not with it, and it includes ETX. Getting either end wrong is a common bug in home-made readers.
